Senator Susan Collins's husband has worked for the lobbyist leading the
primary super PAC supporting her re-election campaign in Maine, and he
apparently worked for the lobbyist again last year, documents reviewed by
**Zeteo** show.

According to Collins's most recent financial disclosure, her husband, Tom
Daffron, consulted last year for Chesapeake Enterprises, which appears to be
the [lobbying firm](https://www.opensecrets.org/federal-
lobbying/firms/summary?id=D000032521) based in Dallas, Texas. According to the
form, Daffron was paid more than $1,000. Exact figures do not have to be
disclosed.

The nature of Daffron's work for Chesapeake Enterprises is not clear. A firm
by that name is run by Scott Reed, a
[lobbyist](https://www.citizensforethics.org/reports-investigations/crew-
investigations/scott-reed-finally-starts-following-the-law-after-crew-calls-
him-out/) and former
[strategist](https://www.politico.com/news/2020/09/29/chamber-of-commerce-
strategist-resigns-423123) for the U.S. Chamber of Commerce. Reed is one of
Collins's most important backers: He [chairs](https://zeteo.com/p/fascists-
want-comedian-fired) Pine Tree Results PAC, a pro-Collins super PAC that spent
[$4 million](https://www.fec.gov/data/independent-
expenditures/?data_type=processed&q_spender=C00894709&is_notice=true&most_recent=true&min_date=01%2F01%2F2025&max_date=12%2F31%2F2026)
on negative ads against Democrat Graham Platner even before primary day in
Maine. (Pine Tree Results was formed on Jan. 3, 2025.)

Daffron and Reed, who led a pro-Collins outside group in 2020, worked together
as
[lobbyists](https://lda.gov/filings/public/filing/c19f003e-7d5b-4870-8b34-35073b02df14/print/)
for Chesapeake Enterprises more than two decades ago, with Daffron
[serving](https://www.centralmaine.com/2012/07/29/collins-future-husband-once-
her-mentor_2012-07-28/) as an executive vice president at the firm from 2001
to 2004.
